According to recent reports, A dog's breath is never going to be minty fresh, but there's a major difference between ordinary doggy breath and an odor that's genuinely foul. A healthy dog's mouth should have a mild smell, often with a faint trace of whatever they last ate. When that smell suddenly becomes fishy, rotten, or unusually unpleasant, it can be a sign that something else is going on.

Bad breath can have several possible causes, ranging from common dental problems to health conditions that need urgent veterinary attention. Knowing what that smell might be telling you can make it easier to recognize when it's time for a closer look.

In a recent development, periodontal disease is the most common cause of persistent bad breath in dogs. It develops as tartar builds up on the teeth and eventually affects the ligament holding each tooth in place.

Recent findings suggest that the smell can become particularly strong and rotten as the disease progresses. Other signs include inflamed or bleeding gums, loose or missing teeth, heavy tartar, exposed tooth roots, changes in appetite, difficulty chewing, and pawing at the mouth.

According to recent reports, gingivitis is an earlier stage of periodontal disease and causes the gums to become inflamed. Bad breath is often one of the first noticeable signs.

It has been revealed that unlike more advanced periodontal disease, gingivitis is reversible when treated. A professional dental cleaning combined with regular dental care at home can usually address the problem. Without treatment, however, gingivitis can progress into periodontal disease and eventually contribute to tooth loss.

According to recent reports, sometimes the mouth isn't where the problem starts. Digestive conditions can also affect the way a dog's breath smells.

Gastroenteritis, acid reflux, food intolerances, intestinal blockages, and even gastrointestinal cancer can all be associated with changes in breath odor. Many of these conditions can cause vomiting, which leaves behind a sharp, sour smell from bile.

Acid reflux can also produce a similar sour odor even when a dog isn't actually vomiting.

It has been revealed that what a dog eats can have a noticeable effect on breath. It's perfectly normal for some of the smell of a dog's food to linger after a meal, but certain diets can leave a much stronger odor behind.

It has been revealed that seafood and fish oil supplements, for example, can give a dog's breath a distinctly fishy smell. Dogs that eat feces, whether their own or another animal's, can also develop particularly foul breath afterward. This behavior, known as coprophagia, is unpleasant but fairly common.

Bad breath isn't always caused by the teeth or gums. The oral cavity also includes the jaw bones, tongue, soft palate, and the inside of the cheeks, and problems affecting any of these areas can produce an unpleasant smell.

Industry observers note that injuries can become infected and lead to tissue damage, creating the odor associated with the breakdown of damaged tissue. Tumors can also develop in these areas and may cause similar tissue damage and bad breath.

According to recent reports, A sweet or fruity smell coming from a dog's breath can have a very different explanation. In a diabetic dog, it can be a sign of ketoacidosis, a serious complication that occurs when the body doesn't have enough insulin and begins burning fat for energy instead.

This process produces ketones, which can become toxic as they accumulate in the blood. The resulting breath can have a sweet, fruity smell that is sometimes compared with acetone.

Interestingly, not everyone can smell ketones on a dog's breath. Differences in how people perceive smells, including genetic differences in scent perception, may explain why the odor is more noticeable to some people than others.

Kidney disease can give a dog's breath a distinct ammonia-like smell.

Healthy kidneys filter waste products such as urea from the bloodstream so they can be removed from the body through urine. When kidney function is impaired, urea can build up in the blood instead.

That excess urea eventually reacts with saliva and converts to ammonia, producing the distinctive smell that can be noticeable on a dog's breath.

Industry observers note that an unpleasant smell coming from a dog's mouth doesn't always originate anywhere near the mouth. In fact, the problem could be at the opposite end!

According to recent reports, impacted or infected anal glands can cause a dog to lick or nibble the area in an attempt to relieve the discomfort. Anal gland fluid often has an intensely fishy smell, and when a dog licks the area, that odor can transfer directly to the mouth and breath.

Persistent bad breath is worth investigating rather than simply trying to cover up the smell. The underlying cause could be as manageable as dental disease, but it can also be associated with more serious health problems.

Regular brushing and professional dental cleanings can help prevent periodontal disease, which is the most common cause of ongoing bad breath in dogs.

A sudden change in breath odor deserves particular attention, especially if it appears alongside other changes such as appetite problems, vomiting, or repeated licking at a particular part of the body. In those situations, a vet can help determine what's causing the smell and whether anything else needs to be treated.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Packing a lunchbox snack shouldn’t require a degree, but the snack aisle makes a decent case otherwise.

It has been revealed that labels promise real fruit, no artificial anything and a good source of something. The truth is, most of it is noise. The part that matters is on the nutrition label. For a run of dietitian-approved lunchbox snacks you can buy and pack as-is, we asked two registered dietitians who shop that aisle for a living what they actually look for.

Sources indicate that robin Barrie Kaiden, MS, RD, CDN, CSSD and Lauren Manaker, MS, RDN, LD, both do the same thing with a new product before it goes in the cart: They turn it over and read. Here’s what they’re looking for, and the snacks they reach for without overthinking it.

Kaiden scans the label’s ingredients first. “That matters to me more than anything else,” she states. She wants simple, real-food ingredients and the least processed option available. There’s a practical reason to start there, notes Manaker. Ingredients appear in order by weight, so the first few make up most of the product.

The claims on the front get much less of their attention. “Made with real fruit” doesn’t tell you how much fruit is actually in there, says Kaiden, and “no artificial flavors” doesn’t automatically make something a nourishing snack. Even the regulated claims are narrower than they sound, explains Manaker. “Good source of fiber” means the product provides 10 to 19% of the daily value per serving. “Gluten free” matters for kids with celiac disease or a gluten sensitivity and does nothing nutritionally for anyone else.

The label lists added sugars and total sugars separately. Total sugars include the naturally occurring sugars in ingredients like fruit and milk, claims Manaker. Added sugars are the ones put in during processing, and those are the numbers to take into consideration. The targets for added sugar are lower than most parents expect. The Dietary Guidelines for Americans recommend no added sugars for children under 10, and the American Academy of Pediatrics advises less than 25 grams, about 6 teaspoons, per day for kids 2 and older.

Sources indicate that kaiden also looks at where the sugar comes from. She passes on high-fructose corn syrup and would rather see a small amount of honey, maple syrup or coconut sugar. “Those are still added sugars, so the amount matters, but the source and processing matter to me, too,” she states. If cane sugar is on the list, she prefers it farther down.

Protein and fiber make a massive difference in how satisfying a snack is. Kaiden balances a carbohydrate-rich food with protein and some healthy fat, like fruit with nuts, cheese or plain yogurt. “That combination helps slow digestion and supports steadier energy through the afternoon,” she notes. For a substantial afternoon snack, she suggests around 5 to 10 grams of protein and at least 3 grams of fiber, depending on a child’s age, appetite and activity level. Those numbers can come from the snack as a whole. No single bar has to do everything.

Most U.S. children don’t get the recommended amount of fiber, notes Manaker, so small additions help. Fruit, veggies, beans, whole-grain bread or crackers, and nuts or seeds where school rules allow are all easy lunchbox sources.

Sources indicate that hydrogenated and partially hydrogenated oils are an automatic no for Kaiden. Partially hydrogenated oils contain industrial trans fats, which are particularly harmful to heart health. High-fructose corn syrup, a highly processed sweetener that adds sugar without meaningful nutrition, is another pass.

Seed oils get a lot of negative press, but Kaiden’s position helps clear up confusion: When there’s a comparable option, she opts for extra virgin olive oil or avocado oil instead of seed oils because of the difference in processing. Many seed oils are extensively refined, and some are extracted using solvents such as hexane. “That processing is why I personally prefer other options,” she indicates, “not because all seed oils are harmful or because using hexane means unsafe amounts remain in the food.”.

Sources indicate that she’s also not rigid about it. Some Simple Mills crackers contain sunflower oil, and she still buys them for the almond-flour base. “I look at the whole product rather than letting one ingredient make the decision for me,” she says.

It has been revealed that unfamiliar names aren’t automatically a problem, either. Ascorbic acid is vitamin C. Tocopherols are forms of vitamin E that can help preserve freshness. “I care more about what an ingredient actually is than whether its name is easy to pronounce,” indicates Kaiden.

Read the ingredients even on brands you buy regularly, Kaiden cautions, because formulations change, and one good product doesn’t mean everything from that brand makes the cut.

To make shopping easier for you, we asked the nutritionists exactly what they’re tossing in their carts. Take notes!

Kaiden’s favorite snack doesn’t sound like a dietitian’s pick at all. “Potato chips!” she says, naming José Andrés Extra Virgin Olive Oil Potato Chips, made with potatoes, extra virgin olive oil and salt. “I want my kids to enjoy their food, and a simple-ingredient chip can absolutely fit into a balanced lunchbox. Add a sandwich and some fruit or vegetables, and you have a lunch that’s nourishing and enjoyable.” Potato chips? Say less.

Our four kittens â one female, three males â lost their mommy just after they turned two months old. They were already raiding her food bowl to munch on her dry kibble. Since mommy passed away from mastitis, they have developed a habit of trying to suckle on one another. I have seen each kitten do this.

We tried to separate them as soon as we see them doing this, but nothing works.

Recent findings suggest that what can we do to help stop this? â.

I am so sorry these babies lost their mama so suddenly. They have essentially decided, âNo Mom? Fine, weâll improvise!â.

What you are seeing is called non-nutritive suckling, and in orphaned kittens, it can be surprisingly persistent. It is not necessarily hunger at this age. Suckling is also a built-in comfort behavior, and losing their mother can leave them looking for another way to satisfy that need. Research in orphaned kittens has specifically documented cross-suckling between littermates, with a higher risk in kittens that lost their mother.

Rather than simply trying to stop the behavior, you could give them an appropriate place to redirect it. There has been research into providing a âsurrogate motherâ for orphaned kittens, essentially a soft plush object fitted with artificial nipples, sometimes described as a kitten pacifier or nursing station. The idea is lovely because it gives them an outlet for that very normal suckling drive while allowing the siblings to continue enjoying their important social contact. I would look for a purpose-designed kitten nursing surrogate or a very soft, durable, washable object specifically intended for this use, rather than improvising with anything that could shed fibers, unravel, or be swallowed.

In a recent development, it is also worth knowing that some cats never completely give up their âbaby habit.â Suckling can persist into adulthood and may be directed toward blankets, clothing, plastics, themselves, siblings, or other cats, and even towards the owners. In many cats, it is simply a comforting ritual, but it becomes a concern if they chew and swallow fabric or fur, or if another cat develops irritated or injured skin. So for these four little characters, the goal does not necessarily have to be âstop suckling forever.â It is more about teaching them, âHere is your approved place to do that.â.

It has been revealed that most importantly, keep an eye on the areas they are currently targeting. Suckling around the belly or especially the genital area can cause significant irritation and injury, so those kittens should be separated from the suckler when necessary and examined for redness, swelling, hair loss, wounds, or difficulty urinating.

It has been revealed that with a safe alternative, plenty of play and enrichment, and gentle redirection, they may gradually outgrow the behavior, or they may simply become those adult cats who still insist on having their favorite comfort blanket. Some cats do have a talent for keeping their childhood traditions!

Where a cartoonistâs path diverges from that of wiser, more sensible humans is that we love the process of creating more than we chafe at the frustration. Believe me, there is frustration. Industry observers note that I grew up in a small lake community, but Shag was found by my grandpa just living on the streets of Detroit. He was pretty feral â Shag, not my grandpa â and impossible to train, but also a total sweetheart. They slept in the garage, and in the morning weâd often find him sleeping on top of the car. Tigger, on the other hand, preferred to sleep behind the toilet. And he wasnât a small dog.

In any case, I believe these two funny mutts had as much influence on my work as any other cartoonist.

Great question! Cats and dogs are obviously very different, but they have one really big thing in common: their own unique personalities. Thatâs what makes both perfect for cartoons â most of us already treat them like little furry people anyway, right? Itâs just their behaviors that set them apart.

Recent findings suggest that there are two aspects to dog cartoons: The first and most obvious is that they really arejokes about dogsâ behavior in general â how they eat, how they might react in different settings, why they lick themselves, bathroom habits, etc etc. Thereâs a lot of material there! The second aspect is what generates even more material, and thatâs when dogs are reflecting human behavior, or simply behaving like a human.

Bad dog!â In the background, her husband (presumably) shakes back and forth like the toy. At some level, the cartoon is about the coupleâs relationship, right? But itâs framed by a typical and humorous dog action weâve all seen before. Just not with a voodoo doll, haha.

I would say simply that our question is also the answer: love. I try to approach my cartoons the same way I approach dogs in real life; from a standpoint of love, affection, admiration, and a little bit of gratitude that they exist.

I think of that often: when I share a cartoon, the reader brings their own life experiences to it and then weâve made a two-way connection. That connection is my favorite part of the gig.

According to recent reports, my only hope is that my cartoons help people simply see the world in a different way for a few seconds. I want them to laugh with others and not at others; see that absurdities are universal and that when we recognize ourselves or others in a cartoon, weâre really just acknowledging that weâre all connected.

I Take A Sedative To Fall Asleep Every Night & I Have No Intention Of Stopping

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1185 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Scarymommy

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I don’t care if I’m reliant on it and you can’t make me.
  • Sleep deprivation is a form of torture.
  • Industry observers note that as a kid, I remember lying in bed for long stretches of time before I could fall asleep.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I don’t care if I’m reliant on it and you can’t make me.

Sleep deprivation is a form of torture. At some point in every adult’s life, you find out why the hard way. Every parent goes through intense sleep deprivation when they bring home their first baby, and every subsequent newborn after that. But for some of us, sleep never came easy. By the time the babies came on the scene, we were well acquainted with the wee hours of the morning, what it felt like to be up all night, every night.

Industry observers note that as a kid, I remember lying in bed for long stretches of time before I could fall asleep. My thoughts would race about everything and nothing. I had a dream catcher above my bed to ward off nightmares, worry dolls under my pillow to whisper my anxieties to so they could “hold them for me” until the morning, and my bedroom TV volume on low while a plucky Disney Channel show played. At sleepovers I was always the last to fall asleep, if I managed to stay overnight at all.

Industry observers note that I didn’t get a formal anxiety diagnosis until I went off to college many years later, but learning more about my brain finally gave me an understanding of why sleep was so elusive. With a nervous system stuck in fight-or-flight mode, of course I’d wake at the slightest sound and have a nearly impossible time winding down enough to knock out at the end of the day.

Finally, in 2019, I expressed my frustrations to my upcoming psychiatrist. I was awake for hours every night waiting for sleep to come, while my husband was already in REM before he ever got fully horizontal on the mattress. I tried guided meditations (why do all the beach ones feature squawking seagulls?) and binaural beats and exercising with the goal of exhausting myself during the day, but my insomnia had reached a frustrating new intensity. It was making my anxiety and depression so much worse; I looked and felt utterly bedraggled. So, he prescribed me trazodone.

While trazodone isn’t a true sedative — it’s actually an antidepressant — it’s often used off-label to treat insomnia because it gives you a similar relaxing, drowsy feeling. My doctor told me that it’s not a controlled substance and carries a very low risk of addiction, but that mentally, I might start to feel like I need it in order to sleep. If I didn’t like feeling dependent on it, we could make some changes.

“Are they going to stop making it any time soon?” I asked.

“Is it bad to take long-term for any other reason?”.

Sources indicate that “Then I’m perfectly fine with being mentally addicted,” I mentioned. And I’ve taken it every single night since then.

Research has shown again and again that regularly sleeping well is a key quality-of-life indicator. Lack of sleep negatively impacts every system of the body, weakening the immune system, worsening mental health, and increasing risk of countless conditions, from high cholesterol to Alzheimer’s. Women are twice as likely to have insomnia as men, which has been attributed to our natural hormonal fluctuations throughout the month and the fact that we tend to carry the lion’s share of the mental load in the family, on top of being more prone to mood disorders.

Recent findings suggest that yet even though we know all of this, taking anything to help you fall asleep is still... kind of frowned upon. Researchers in the UK conducted focus groups interviewing people who take prescription sleep medications and OTC supplements, like melatonin, and found that they had a lot of internalized stigma around the subject — even when talking about it in a room full of people who also take something to help them sleep.

According to recent reports, they found that participants were very deliberate in how they explained their need for their meds. They’re deserving (explaining that their condition, like chronic pain or anxiety, makes sleep impossible without medication). They’re compliant, only ever taking their meds exactly as prescribed (or, in the case of supplements, as directed on the label). They’re responsible, always watching themselves for signs of addiction or misuse. They expressed extreme guilt over taking more of their medications than they should, or trying alternative medications meant to make them sleepy when their usual prescription wasn’t enough.

We recently asked Scary Mommy’s Instagram followers the question, “Do you take anything to fall asleep at night?” Some of that same stigma showed up in their responses too.

It has been revealed that multiple readers noted they take Gravol when they can’t sleep, calling it a “horrid habit” or something they only do “when things get really bad.” Another said, “I can’t sleep without a quarter of an Ambien. It’s terrible!” “Haven’t had an unmedicated sleep in 7+ years 🫠,” said one response. The melting face is doing a lot of heavy lifting there.

Of course there were plenty of Scary Mommies who felt no shame (that’s sort of our shtick around here). In response to the question “Do you take anything to fall asleep?” one user simply replied, “WINE.” Plenty of other respondents also take trazodone, or Unisom, or some other sleep aid. Weed, whether in vape or gummy form, is also an extremely popular option. See also: a large number of replies indicating they take magnesium and progesterone at night thanks to perimenopause, and that HRT was finally the thing to help them sleep through the night.

But one response really captures my feelings about the whole subject:.

Sources indicate that “Oh lord I’m so medicated. But it’s working.”.

Even on the days I feel like I shouldn’t have to take something to help me sleep, that perhaps I could sleepmaxx or wellness hack my way out of having to take a pill every night, I remind myself that not getting enough sleep is literally deadly.

When you’re someone who struggles with sleep night after night, you know how swiftly your mental and physical health can plummet. Insomnia decimates my quality of life. Sleep deprivation locks my personality and my joy away behind a concrete wall where I can’t access them anymore. It impacts my longevity and my relationships. While I’m not saying every reader who responded has a healthy way of getting to sleep at night, or that we shouldn’t be critical of our relationships with substances, I think we could all use a little validation that not getting enough sleep is, in fact, torturous.

More moms need to hear that they deserve to sleep well. They should know that their doctors want to hear from them if they feel abnormally tired during the day. And I want more women to internalize the idea that this world is hard enough to live in as it is. You should at least be able to meet it each day not feeling like a shell of yourself.

And that’s why you can pry my trazodone out of my cold, dead hands.

#32664. This year’s top-searched holiday toys will make your Millennial heart sing

This year’s top-searched holiday toys will make your Millennial heart sing

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (445 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Mother

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Each November, Google gives us a peek behind the curtain, synthesising billions of shopping-related searches into their Holiday 100 Gift Guide.
  • Here are the trending toys parents will want to know about, plus what the list says about how we’re shopping this year.
  • Searches for “classic toy train set” climbed 240% this year, one of the biggest jumps Google shared.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Each November, Google gives us a peek behind the curtain, synthesising billions of shopping-related searches into their Holiday 100 Gift Guide. The list is built from a full year of Search trends across every category from tech to style. And this year, the toys and games section looks suspiciously like the inside of an elder millennial’s childhood toy chest.

Here are the trending toys parents will want to know about, plus what the list says about how we’re shopping this year.

Searches for “classic toy train set” climbed 240% this year, one of the biggest jumps Google shared. Wooden trains survive toddler teeth, being thrown down the stairs and never fail to get passed down more than once. (Expect the figure-eight to claim your living room floor for the next few years.).

“A ton of play,” Google wrote, and we respect the pun. Searches for stuffed elephant plushies rose 240%, with the Pets Alive Baby Elephant Surprise as the featured pick. Plush is a good pick for a 1-year-old and a 10-year-old alike, and the right one becomes a friend for life.

Searches for the Fujifilm instax holiday set jumped 190%. For tweens, a camera that spits out a real photo is a nice break from the phone, and the prints end up taped to bedroom walls instead of buried in a camera roll. They’ll fly through the film, so tuck a couple of extra packs in the box.

According to recent reports, searches for the FAO Schwarz Piano Mat “struck a chord,” rising 180% in 2026. Anyone who watched Tom Hanks stomp out a duet on the giant keyboard in “Massive” wanted one of these, and the floor-sized version now fits in a playroom. It’s a sneaky music-and-movement toy for preschoolers. It’s also loud, so choose its permanent residence carefully.

Searches for “adjustable roller skates” cruised up 180%. Adjustable skates expand across several sizes, so they can outlast a growth spurt or two. Just remember to add a helmet and pads to the cart.

Some of this may come down to who’s doing the shopping. Millennials make up a significant share of today’s parents, and plenty of us spent our childhoods at the roller rink, building wooden train tracks across the living room rug and waiting for Polaroids to develop. (By impatiently wagging them back and forth, of course.) It’s not hard to imagine a few of these searches coming from parents trying to hand down something that felt magic to them. The best part? There’s a good chance they’ll all still be in rotation when next year’s list comes out.

Check out the full Toys & Games list here!

Latest Update: 29 Gifts For Moms Whose Favorite Form Of Therapy Is Travel

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2879 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Scarymommy

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some clichés are clichés for a reason.
  • According to recent reports, so, when it comes to gifts you can give the moms in your life, it’s hard to beat travel gifts...
  • Here are some of our favorite travel-forward finds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You can never go wrong with travel gifts, TBH.

Some clichés are clichés for a reason. Being a mom is really hard. But it’s so, so rewarding. Also, travel is the best teacher. For many moms, those three clichés are often true in tandem. Sometimes, the lessons we learn during travel make the invisible load of motherhood a little lighter to bear. Sometimes, the lesson is simply that we have to make time for ourselves to be the best moms we can be. And sometimes, seeing the world through our kids’ eyes is enough to remind us that even when the road is rough, the reward is usually worth it.

According to recent reports, so, when it comes to gifts you can give the moms in your life, it’s hard to beat travel gifts... especially when travel already seems to be their favorite form of therapy. While splurging on things as pricey as plane tickets or an all-inclusive resort stay is (understandably) out of reach for many of us, there are tons of items any travel-loving mom would be overjoyed to get. We should know! The Scary Mommy editors are all busy moms who enjoy squeezing getaways and adventures into whatever little pockets of spare time we can find.

Here are some of our favorite travel-forward finds.

It has been revealed that I have the full-size Naturepedic pillow, and I yearn to own the travel-sized one too. I have chronic neck pain and headaches, so I need a soft yet supportive pillow and one that is comfortable when sleeping on my back or my side. I’ve purchased and used so many pillows in my day, and this is finally THE ONE. I love that you can customize how much stuffing you keep inside, and I like to form mine with a little divot for my head to maximize my neck support. The full-size is heavy, though, so I really want to find a travel-sized one under the tree this year to use instead of the down (deeply unsupportive) hotel pillows that leave me hurting. — Katie McPherson, Associate Editor, Lifestyle & Entertainment.

It has been revealed that this is the diaper bag I wish I’d had for every family trip with little ones! It fits a pump, bottles, diapers, a laptop... really, you’d be surprised how much stuff you can stuff in it. I especially love that there’s a quick-grab pocket on the front sized perfectly for wipes. Even though my kids are teens, I carry this as a carry-on backpack because it’s so pretty and functional, and it slips right over your suitcase handle so you have one less thing to juggle at the gate. Thanks to the easy-clean neoprene and chic design, it doesn’t scream “diaper bag.” — Julie Sprankles, Deputy Editor, Lifestyle & Entertainment.

Sources indicate that the Cincha Go-Tote has become my most-reached-for travel bag because it solves the one problem every traveler has: The carry-on that tips over every time you let go of it. The Cincha Go-Tote has a built-in luggage sleeve that slides right over your suitcase handle so everything stays put, and your hands stay free; plus it is water-resistant, has leather accents that make it look way more elevated than a travel bag has any right to look, and fits everything you need for a flight without becoming a black hole. This is for the traveler on your holiday list who has everything but still somehow does not have this. — Katie Garrity, Senior Editor, News & Social.

I have bought my fair share of travel pillows over the years, and a lot of them just... don't get the job done. I love this one because it stuffs into a small sack and it really does help you nod off on the plane without choking or smothering you. When I travel with this, people always ask me where it's from. — Sarah Aswell, Deputy Editor, News & Social.

I think my new favorite obsession is traveling with a trunk! For those trips when you need the extra space, this beauty lets you travel in style. It has such a sophisticated vintage-inspired look... it feels like it should be loaded onto the Orient Express. That old-world glamour even extends to a sleek double-latch closure (instead of a zipper) with TSA-approved locks. She’s not just pretty, though; she’s durable too, thanks to a tough polycarbonate shell, reinforced corners, and replaceable wheels. And once you get used to traveling trunk-style with its super-convenient deep side, it’ll be hard to go back! — Julie Sprankles.

Sources indicate that packing for a trip with kids usually means digging through a black hole for one sock, and these clear, color-coded organizers fix that. The set of four comes in major, medium, and mini sizes with windows so you can see exactly what’s inside, and my favorite part is that each one gets its own job, like clothes, snacks, or tech and first aid. They’re the unglamorous travel upgrade that makes packing and unpacking take minutes instead of hours, and I’m never traveling without them again!— Katie Garrity.

I don't know how many times I've had a fully charged battery back with me while traveling, but I can't find the right cord to attach it to my phone. This magnetic charger is small, mighty, and charges cordlessly! It has become my number one charging brick, and that says a lot coming from me. This is one of those products where you buy one and then almost immediately buy another one, just to have a spare. I also love getting these as gifts for people! — Sarah Aswell.

According to recent reports, my non-negotiable for travel days is comfort, but I don’t want to look like I rolled right out of bed and onto the plane, either. These Cozy Earth joggers are just the ticket. They’re ridiculously soft, with a slim-but-relaxed fit and an adjustable drawstring that’s perfect for long flights. And the burgundy color is seriously stunning, so I look put-together even though I feel like I’m in my comfiest PJs. — Julie Sprankles.

Ask anyone who knows me, and they'll tell you my happy place is sitting out in the sun — wherever that may be. As someone who has long loved Gray Malin's art (but not someone who has been able to splurge on it as often as I'd like), these travel pouches make a great happy medium. I love how packable and useful these travel pouches are, but what I love most about them is how "in the mood" they'll get you to travel. As you pack up your stuff, you can practically taste vacation. What's not to love? — Kate Auletta, Editor in Chief.

It has been revealed that for the traveler on your list who is still hauling around a beat-up suitcase, this is the upgrade that will make them feel like a seasoned jet-setter, with a slim aluminum frame and polycarbonate shell that look as sleek as they are tough. The 77-liter interior has a built-in compression panel for squeezing in just a little more and about 1.5 inches of extra depth, which is exactly what you need for a 7- to 10-day trip. It also has 360° spinner wheels and two TSA-approved locks, so it’s the gift that makes every airport trip a little less stressful! — Katie Garrity.

In a recent development, like many people entering their 40s after a lifetime of wear and tear, I deal with a lot of foot complications, especially when I'm walking 20,000 steps a day while traveling. I love these shoe inserts that have gotten me through the most epic travel days, including 12-mile days at Disney World and a 15-mile day hike in Glacier National Park. — Sarah Aswell.

While experts generally agree that airlines don’t reuse blankets, it’s still comforting just to carry your own on board. As someone who is always cold, I can’t tell you how much I appreciate being able to toss this into my carry-on. It comes with a super-soft throw, a matching eye mask, and the coordinating bag to stash them both in. — Julie Sprankles.

Industry observers note that this is the carry-on to match all carry-ons! This backpack opens super wide at the top so you can find anything you need, plus it has a large front zippered pocket for chargers, snacks, or notes from admirers. It fits so much stuff and yet still somehow slides perfectly under an airplane seat like some kind of backpack sorcery. — Katie Garrity.

It’s just designed to fit so much more, even though it takes up the same amount of space as other bags. Used with the packing cubes from the same company, I can easily fit a week’s worth of stuff into a bag and not have to check anything. — Sarah Aswell.

Marshall is such an iconic brand that I feel a little cooler every time I slip these headphones on. There are lots of reasons they’re great for tossing in your carry-on. The adaptive noise cancellation automatically blocks out plane noises, but one push of a button switches to transparency mode so I can hear flight announcements. The battery lasts up to 50-plus hours with ANC on. And, one of my favorite features, they’re made to fold up small so you can stash them in your bag without a hassle. — Julie Sprankles.

This tote organizer turns any bottomless pit of a bag into an orderly dream. With pockets and pouches for all of your on-the-go essentials, the ToteSavvy makes traveling a breeze. — Katie Garrity.

It has been revealed that S'well makes my favorite lunch salad bowl container; it never leaks and is super high-quality. So when I saw that the same company came out with a travel bottle set, I knew that I wanted it! All of their products are so well-designed and thoughtful; these bottles are made of lightweight material, and they haven't leaked yet. They also come in a super cute lightweight pouch. — Sarah Aswell.

Industry observers note that my husband travels for work, so he flies multiple times per week. He’s been using the Airback MAX for about a year now, and it has held up remarkably well to his strenuous schedule! But what he really loves is that it lets him skip checking a bag because it has a built-in vacuum system that sucks air out of your clothes. That means you can fit 25+ items in this one carry-on-sized bag. It also converts from a rolling trolley to a backpack in seconds, has dual TSA-approved locks, USB ports, and an expandable compression bag that doubles as a laundry bag. — Julie Sprankles.

According to recent reports, the scariest part of any flight is wondering how long the entertainment is going to last, and this kit is built to keep toddlers 18 months and up busy from takeoff to landing without a single screen. It comes with a first-flight storybook that helps set expectations before you board, which is a small thing that makes a major difference when a little one has never been on a plane. It’s compact, screen-free, and designed by Lovevery’s play experts, so it’s one more thing I don’t have to worry about in the carry-on. — Katie Garrity.

For a bag that barely weighs a pound when unpacked and tucks away neatly into a small zippered square, you’ll be shocked by how much The Foldie actually holds: When fully expanded, it has a 40-liter packing volume. The expandable bottom adds just the right amount of extra space when needed. We love that it’s a great size to use as your carry-on or to tuck into your suitcase for bringing home souvenirs. I’ve been using this bag heavily for almost two years now, and it’s still one of my absolute favorites. Not only does it still look great, but I get asked about it all the time! — Julie Sprankles.

In a recent development, I fully admit I got one of these after seeing a social media video of a before-and-after. This thing really does depuff your face... and if you're like me, my face can get pretty puffy while traveling. Carrying this with me and having it after I get off the plane or after a long car ride just makes me feel better. And even besides the de-puffing benefits, it feels really good, too. — Sarah Aswell.

Sources indicate that I love that the Woda is the brainchild of two moms living in Charleston, South Carolina, who needed something hands-free that could be hosed down after days on the coast with their kids. For moms who love to pack up the car and head to the nearest beach as much as possible, you can’t get a better gift than this super-durable yet lightweight waterproof backpack. Made from a non-toxic EVA foam, it’s mold- and mildew-resistant, meaning she won’t have to worry about it getting funky after a day on the water. And it’s seriously roomy with a carrying capacity of up to 30 pounds! — Julie Sprankles.

Industry observers note that any traveler knows long flights cause blood flow in the legs to slow down since you’re seated for extended periods. That, in turn, can increase the risk of health challenges like deep vein thrombosis. Compression socks are a simple way to help blood vessels work more efficiently on long flights, reducing the risk of swelling and blood clots. Trust us when we say that Dr. Motion compression socks are out here compressioning! And they come in so many cute patterns, which is so girly to say... but we don’t care. — Katie Garrity.

In a recent development, what did I do before packing cubes? I love these by JanSport because they are larger than most and fit perfectly in my suitcase side by side. The smaller "cube" is great for carrying an extra pair of undies and a spare shirt in my carry-on. They also have a see-through mesh front and a carrying handle, which make a huge difference. And never forget that JanSport items all come with an incredibly wonderful lifetime warranty. — Sarah Aswell.

Industry observers note that I’m a carry-on girlie whenever I can be, but some trips just require more space. And if I’m going to be checking a bag, I want it to fit everything without being too cumbersome. This Monos Medium Check-in is the perfect size because it’s roomy without being obnoxiously big. Plus, the limited-edition Mulberry color is a deep, glossy purple that is beyond dreamy! Add in the fact that it’s durable, has a TSA-accepted lock, and super-glidable wheels, and I genuinely get excited at the mere thought of packing for my next trip. — Julie Sprankles.

Sources indicate that it’s a toss-up when it comes to what’s more vexing: using generic hotel bar soap to wash your face or having to buy latest face wash when you get where you’re going because you can’t carry on your fave. That’s why I’m a substantial fan of Olay Cleansing Melts. These portable cleansing squares are TSA-friendly since they’re water-activated, so you can toss ‘em in your purse or carry-on. — Kate Auletta.

It has been revealed that raise your hand if you’ve ever frantically patted down every pocket in an airport security line, convinced you lost your passport (me, it’s definitely me). So when I needed a latest passport holder, I knew I wanted one with a bit of built-in peace of mind. This Spotminders Passport Holder Air works with Apple’s Find My app, meaning I can see exactly where my passport is in about two seconds. It’s ultra-slim but still has room for my license and a few other cards, plus a dedicated flap for boarding passes. Right now there’s a buy-two-get-one-free deal, which makes it a smart pick if you’re looking to upgrade the whole family before a big trip. — Julie Sprankles.

Recent findings suggest that for anyone who’s ever stood at the airport counter pulling a sweater out of an overstuffed suitcase, the BÉIS Large Check-In Roller is a game changer, thanks to its built-in weight indicator that tells you when you’re hitting 50 pounds before you ever leave the house. It has a durable hard-shell exterior, 360° wheels, a TSA lock, a hidden AirTag pocket, and 2 inches of expansion for the souvenirs you absolutely will bring home, and the glossy mint color means you’ll spot it on the carousel from across the room. It’s the one piece of luggage that makes a two-week family trip feel organized instead of chaotic! — Katie Garrity.

Industry observers note that for trips when I don’t have room for over-ear headphones, these Nothing Ear (3a) earbuds pack a ton of travel-ready power into a punchy, pocket-sized case. They have active noise cancellation and hi-res sound, plus the battery life is up to 41 hours so I don’t have to hunt for an outlet at the gate. They’re also great for using while on calls. I got the yellow colorway, and it just makes me happy every time I pull them out. — Julie Sprankles.

Breaking: The Top 10 Books Of 2026, According To Amazon (& Scary Mommy) Editors

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, countless new books come out every single year, and your TBR just gets longer and longer (and longer).
  • According to recent reports, “An extraordinary Trojan horse of a novel that will make your heart sing and make you want to talk to everybody you know about it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some Scary Mommy Editor favorites made the list too.

According to recent reports, countless new books come out every single year, and your TBR just gets longer and longer (and longer). If you’re struggling to figure out what to read before the end of the year, well, here’s some guidance. As they do each year, Amazon’s book editors have selected the best books of the year across all genres, including their top 20 overall. Some you’ve probably heard of and others may have slipped your notice until now, but here are their very top 10 for your consideration before year’s end.

According to recent reports, “An extraordinary Trojan horse of a novel that will make your heart sing and make you want to talk to everybody you know about it. Utterly magnetic, American Hagwon will change the way you think about family, sacrifice, and education. Min Jin Lee has written (another) once-in-a-lifetime read.” —Al Woodworth, Amazon Editor.

Recent findings suggest that devastated by a shocking betrayal, John and Helen Koh move their three children from Seoul to Southern California. Latest opportunity is everywhere for the children, while the elder Kohs find their education and experience in Korea does not translate to the States. As their friends, relatives, and enemies come and go, the family continues “nursing the almost all-consuming faith that education will lead the next generation to success and security.”.

Sources indicate that “A sparkling, genre-busting gift of a novel, Emily St. John Mandel’s latest is dystopian fiction that shook me to my core. Spanning continents, timelines, and perhaps even universes, Exit Party makes for a glorious puzzle, one with pieces that fit together seamlessly.” —Annabel Gutterman, Amazon Editor.

Recent findings suggest that scary Mommy editor Katie Garrity called this novel “mind-bending.” Set in 2031, California has declared itself a republic apart from the U.S. The curfew in Los Angeles lifts for the first time in weeks, and citizens gravitate to a big party. What happens there will haunt Ari Waker, freshly out of prison after 18 years, for years to come.

Sources indicate that “Robert Kolker’s enthralling medical mystery is both mesmerizing and heartbreaking — it asks significant questions about chance and choice, what makes a full life, what we’re willing to run toward (or hide from), and how we care for each other. It’s a true story that will stick with you.” —Lindsay Powers, Amazon Editor.

This is the heartbreaking true story of a family plagued by dementia as early as in their 40s due to a shared genetic mutation. In a family with nine siblings that all strike out as young adults, only the youngest child, Barb, is still home to see her mother become withdrawn and uncaring. Then, one by one, other members of the family begin losing jobs, destroying their marriages, and getting further and further away from their former selves. And it’s Barb who sets out to find answers — and a cure.”.

“This was our pick for the best book of the year so far, and our love for this novel about two motherless friends coming of age in the Jim Crow South endures. A nuanced portrait of friendship, family, and race—Jones's sentences sing.” —Erin Kodicek, Amazon Editor.

In a recent development, if you love Jones’ previous work, you will not be disappointed by Kin, said Scary Mommy editor Sarah Aswell after reading the book in July. It follows Annie and Vernice, who have been best friends and neighbors since they were kids in Honeysuckle, Louisiana. Then, at 18, Vernice heads for Spelman College where she is pulled into a world of aspiration and connection, while Annie sets out into the world to find love and adventure. Where will their journeys take them, and will they come back to each other?

In a recent development, “Walking the line between hysterical and horrifying, this electric psychological thriller ruthlessly takes on cultural appropriation through a delicious cat-and-mouse game like no other. If you’re in a reading slump, Fruit Fly is the cure.” —Abby Abell, Amazon Editor.

Mallory Maddox is a washed-up author who hasn’t put out upcoming work in nearly a decade. All the buzz she worked so hard to earn is fading, and fast. So when she meets Leo, an unhoused addict trading sex for the things he needs, she finds her inspiration. How far will she go to write the perfect, career-saving story?”.

“Never before have a 19th-century mapmaker, a scruffy, loyal dog, and a mysterious copse of trees been more enchanting. O’Farrell delivers a soaring and bewitching tale of family, and how the remote Irish peninsula where they live defines and shapes them, generation after generation.” —Al Woodworth, Amazon Editor.

Scary Mommy editor Sarah Aswell read Land in September and declared this story, about a family surviving Ireland’s Great Hunger who find a mysterious spring in the forest, may be O’Farrell’s best work yet.

“Illuminating and unforgettable, Patrick Radden Keefe’s latest delivers another knockout work of narrative nonfiction, this time telling the shocking story of how a young man got caught up in the dangerous and powerful world of Russian oligarchs and landed at the bottom of the Thames.” —Al Woodworth, Amazon Editor.

Sources indicate that if you love documentaries and true crime podcasts, this book is a must-read. In the wee hours of the morning of November 29, 2019, cameras outside MI6 headquarters captured footage of a young man pacing back and forth before throwing himself into the river Thames. What follows is a deeply reported account of his parents’ quest to get answers about what happened to their son, and how on earth he ended up deciding to jump.

Sources indicate that “The many fans of Major Little Lies will love this follow-up, but you don’t need to have read that book or seen the show to enjoy Big Little Truths. I’ve been a fan of Liane Moriarty since her early books, and this is simply one of her very best. The dialogue is so clever, and the storytelling so engrossing, you won’t be able to put this book down.” —Sarah Gelman, Editorial Director.

Recent findings suggest that here’s how Scary Mommy editor Katie Garrity summed up the book after reading it in August: “Big Little Truths picks up 10 years later with Madeline, Celeste, Jane, Renata, and Bonnie, whose kindergartners are now teenagers navigating drugs, sex, and alcohol, which honestly sounds just as chaotic and stressful as the original but make it high school. When a mysterious stranger starts lurking around the school and the principal receives a severed finger in the mail, old secrets resurface and newly introduced ones threaten to unravel everything.”.

“This heart-pounding, reported memoir sucked me in from the first page; it’s a gripping account of resilience and perseverance that goes far beyond the headlines to reveal what really happened to Evan Gershkovich when he was snatched off the street and thrown into a Russian prison.” —Lindsay Powers, Amazon Editor.

In March 2023, one year after Russia invaded Ukraine, journalist Evan Gershkovich met with a source roughly 900 miles east of Moscow. Out of nowhere, a group of masked agents bursts in, blindfolds him, and abducts him. They tell him he’s being charged as a spy before dumping him in Lefortovo prison. Instead of giving up, Evan kept reporting, all the way up until the prisoner swap that set him free.

“Two-time Pulitzer Prize winner Colson Whitehead delivers another searing page-turner of heists, gangsters, criminals, and families in this mesmerizing portrait of 1980s Upcoming York City.” —Al Woodworth, Amazon Editor.

Recent findings suggest that if you love a good crime novel, don’t skip Cool Machine. It follows Ray Carney, his wife Elizabeth, and partner Pepper through years of heists, body guard gigs, and major transitions in New York’s history. At every turn he comes up against the most violent forces in the city, risking the safety of himself and his family for one more score.

Which of these books just moved straight to the top of your TBR?

Sources indicate that for many cat parents, the brand Capstar might ring a bell. This small, fast-acting tablet has long been used to kill adult fleas on cats and dogs. Now, the active ingredient in Capstar, nitenpyram, is being given an vital upcoming role: treating and preventing New World screwworm.

In a recent development, on September 3, 2026, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA for nitenpyram tablets, allowing the common flea tablet to be used off-label for the prevention and treatment of Fresh World screwworm infestations in cats, kittens, dogs, and puppies.

Why does this matter? Because until now, prevention was the missing piece when it came to drug options for dogs and cats. This new authorization helps fill that gap, giving veterinarians another tool in the toolbox while the larger fight against New World screwworm continues.

First things first: despite the rather dramatic name, New World screwworm is not a worm at all. It is a fly: Cochliomyia hominivorax. The âwormâ part of the name comes from the larvae, or maggot, of this fly. And unfortunately, this is one fly that definitely deserves our attention.

The trouble starts when a female fly finds a suitable place to lay her eggs, usually in or around a wound. She can also target other vulnerable areas, including the eyes, nose, mouth, and other mucous membranes. Once those eggs hatch, the larvae get to work, and this is where the screwworm becomes particularly nasty.

These aren't the disgusting but harmless little maggots that make themselves at home in overflowing trash cans or rotting food. Screwworm larvae feed on living tissue, burrowing deep into the affected area, feeding as they grow. Before long, a wound that looks small on the outside has become a much bigger problem underneath. An infestation can cause extensive tissue damage and, without prompt treatment, can even be life-threatening.

According to recent reports, latest World screwworm has been detected in the United States, while Mexico and other countries in the region continue to deal with the parasite. USDA is maintaining surveillance and response efforts, including in Texas, where âzones of infestationâ have been established.

The concern goes well beyond individual animals. Screwworm can have a serious economic impact on livestock production because affected animals may lose weight, require treatment and extra care, or die. During a 1976 outbreak in Texas, producers spent an estimated $132.1 million dealing with the pest, equivalent to about $740 million in 2024 dollars. More recently, the disruption to live cattle exports from Mexico has been estimated to have cost that country's livestock sector around $1.8 billion.

In a recent development, this is why so much effort is going into keeping this fly from spreading. This is about animal health, but it is also about protecting our entire food production system.

In a recent development, and no, the strategy is not simply âfind the bugs and squish them.â Controlling screwworm takes a much bigger effort. Authorities are using surveillance, movement controls, trapping, and other measures, along with one particularly interesting tool: releasing sterile flies.

In a recent development, the idea is surprisingly simple. Sterile male flies are released into affected areas, where they compete with fertile males for mates. When a sterile male mates with a female, she does not produce viable offspring. Over time, this can cripple the wild screwworm population.

Sources indicate that the good news is that this isn't something every cat owner needs to panic about. Where a cat lives, where it travels, and whether it spends time in an area where screwworm is present all make a difference. For cats traveling to or returning from affected areas, it's worth being a little more careful.

According to recent reports, with screwworm, the goal is to understand the risk before the exposure happens and, whenever possible, st ay one step ahead of the fly. When you consider that cats are experts at hiding things, including small wounds, a puncture, scratch, or other break in the skin can be easy to miss under all that fur, especially in an outdoor cat.

A wound can become an invitation for a female screwworm fly to lay her eggs, and the larvae that hatch will feed on living tissue. Cats infested with screwworm larvae have wounds that aren't healing normally, visible maggots, an unusual odor, or discharge. In any situation, these signs warrant veterinary attention. If you happen to live near or have traveled to an area where the Newly introduced World screwworm has been detected, be sure to mention it to your vet.

Recent findings suggest that not necessarily. This does not mean Capstar should suddenly become part of every cat's routine parasite prevention. As a flea treatment, it is particularly effective at killing adult fleas quickly, but doesnât provide long-term flea control.

It has been revealed that A cat living indoors in an area where screwworm isn't present is in a very different situation from a cat traveling to an affected region or spending time outdoors there. Your veterinarian can help you decide whether your cat's particular situation calls for the medication.

In the case of screwworm, Capstar is used according to the Emergency Use Authorization, not the FDA-approved standard use. There are specific instructions for when and how it should be given.

In a recent development, if you're traveling with your cat to an area where screwworm has been identified, or returning from one, talk with your veterinarian before you go. International travel can also come with health certificates, inspections, and other paperwork, and the requirements vary depending on the country you're entering or passing through. Some documents must be completed within a specific window before travel, so don't leave the paperwork until the last minute.

It has been revealed that for most cats, New World screwworm is not something to worry about every day. But for cats living in or traveling to affected areas, knowing the risk, knowing that preventive options are available, and knowing what to look for can make a real difference. Itâs also great to know that those options include a product that has been safely used in cats for decades.

The takeaway isn't that every cat needs Capstar, but when a parasite like screwworm becomes a concern, having a preventive option available can make it easier to protect cats that are actually at risk.

And when a parasite feeds on living tissue, âbetter safe than sorryâ is a pretty good philosophy.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that this article is sponsored by Eight Sleep. Thank you for supporting the brands that support Motherly and mamas.

Alexandra Zatarain helped build Eight Sleep into a tech unicorn, and she’s expecting her first child in January. Going through pregnancy while running a global firm has reshaped how she sees her own body, her industry and the product she’s building. On this episode of The Motherly Podcast, the co-founder of the sleep-technology company talks about the research that demonstrated Eight Sleep’s technology was improving men’s sleep more than women’s and what the company did about it, why sleep is the most crucial thing women can protect, and the career advice she wishes more women heard before becoming mothers.

Recent findings suggest that meet the expert: Alexandra Zatarain is the co-founder and VP of brand and marketing at Eight Sleep, the sleep-technology manufacturer behind the Pod. The Pod is an intelligent mattress cover that cools or heats each side to your ideal temperature automatically, maximizing deep sleep and minimizing wake-ups. A marketer and brand builder, she grew Eight Sleep from launch into a tech unicorn and helped create what the company calls the sleep fitness movement. Eight Sleep now sells in 37 countries. She’s expecting her first child in January with her husband, Matteo, the company’s co-founder and CEO.

Recent findings suggest that alexandra Zatarain: So many things. I just turned 37, and I’ve seen so many friends go through pregnancy before me. After my first trimester, I felt so bad, thinking, what a terrible friend I was. When you haven’t experienced it, you have such little empathy for what a woman’s body is going through, especially when life keeps demanding so much of you and it doesn’t stop. I really didn’t understand that you could feel so different in your body for so long. It’s built so much more admiration for women and what we go through, and it’s let me embrace a feminine side of myself that in tech you usually don’t get to bring out.

Alexandra Zatarain: It’s made me realize that the only way the world out there is going to change for our benefit as women and mothers is if more of us are the ones making the decisions. I just don’t see any way around it. We have a lot of parents at Eight Sleep, every executive on our team is a parent, but as a woman the experience is completely different. Unless we can share that first-hand knowledge, it’s going to be hard to make progress as fast as we need to. It’s unfortunate that it takes the first-person experience to become that advocate, because everyone should appreciate what mothers go through, given that we all come from a mother.

Recent findings suggest that alexandra Zatarain: A couple of years ago, our clinical team, which is more than 90% women, was analyzing data from our user base and noticed our technology had been improving men’s sleep more than women’s. They asked, what are we missing in how we design this? It turned out the algorithms that manage temperature while you sleep had been fed more data representing men than women. That’s a classic problem in science, where women are underrepresented because our bodies are more complex. You have to account for where someone is in their hormonal journey, pregnancy, postpartum, perimenopause. So we invested a couple million dollars into research and developed features from it. That changed how we think about ourselves, less about helping everyone in a broad way and more about solving specific problems women have had for ages.

Alexandra Zatarain: Sleep is the most vital pillar of health. You would die sooner from sleep deprivation than from food deprivation, which tells you how fundamental it is. For women it matters even more because our hormones rule our lives, and sleep is the one tool we have to regulate them. If you sleep well, your chances of better hormonal balance go up significantly. It’s the best medicine we have, more than working out, more than any meal. The challenge is that those same hormones are often playing against us, making it harder to sleep well in different seasons of life, so keeping our routines as stable as possible helps counter what our bodies are going through.

Alexandra Zatarain: The mindset piece is really important. There’s so much going on, the anxiety, the intrusive thoughts, so not being too hard on yourself is the first step. Understanding that the season will pass should put you a little more at ease, because it’s not going to be your life forever. The other piece is setting yourself up with the right systems, and the most important one is available to everyone for free, which is routine. It helps your body a lot. When you do need to sleep, it’ll be easier for your body to fall asleep because it’s used to the schedule.

Alexandra Zatarain: I’m very rigid about my sleep schedule. I travel a lot, so sleep is number one for me. I make space for eight to nine hours every night, and I’m pretty good at hitting it. I go to bed by 9:30 or 10 every single night no matter where I am in the world, and I don’t really use an alarm unless I have to wake up before 6, because my body just wakes up on its own. That schedule is the thing that’s changed my life the most. Second to that is the environment, the temperature in my room and my bed, the lights going dark, no noise.

Alexandra Zatarain: I think of myself as an athlete, and we’re all sort of athletes in a way. My sport is making decisions about how to build this business, and that means I have to train, stay healthy and think long term. It’s not a sprint. We’ve been doing this for 12 years, so the question is how do I not burn out and stay here 20 or 30 years more. I’m also lucky I built this with my husband, so there’s no real line between business and personal life for us. It’s all mixed in, but it’s so purpose-driven that achieving that purpose every day is what feeds the energy.

Industry observers note that alexandra Zatarain: I’m very open with them about how intentional I was. I did my embryo freezing in my early 30s because of where I was in life. And I tell them that if they want a career after they have a family, the best time to build equity in that career is to push as hard as you can before. Know what you want, because time isn’t always on our side as women. Move up the ranks, so that by the time you have kids you have more flexibility and maybe a higher income. It is possible, but it takes planning, it will require compromises, and very importantly it will require the right partner.

Alexandra Zatarain: It starts with the people around you understanding what you truly need. Sometimes it’s as simple as the encouragement of, yes, go take a nap, yes, your body’s going through a lot. It gets harder once the baby’s home and the mom is maybe exclusively breastfeeding, because it really all falls on you. So have a plan in place ahead of time for how the load is going to be shared. Our partners are much more involved than previous generations, so have those conversations early. It doesn’t end with the birth plan. That’s where everything starts.

It has been revealed that alexandra Zatarain: The first trimester was difficult, a lot of nausea, and it was very hard to function at the level I’m used to. I almost never get sick, so feeling sick every day was a huge shift. It put me in the trajectory to build the team that would make it possible for me to become a mother, to figure out what to delegate and who to elevate, and I’ve built a stronger team as a result. But the biggest thing is that it’s taught me to let go. I can’t control how I feel every day. As a Type A person I always want to be in control, and this has been like therapy, learning that I’m not in control of my body. I’m building a human, and it’s fine if for this season things just work differently.

Who’s a Scaredy Cat? Keeping Cats Safe This Halloween

📅 21 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1165 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Catster

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Catster is reader-supported. When you buy via links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission at no cost to you. Learn more.

According to recent reports, halloween can be an exciting night for families, but all that activity can leave cats feeling unsettled. Strange costumes, unfamiliar visitors, and a doorbell that rings non-stop can be overwhelming, even for cats that usually enjoy meeting upcoming people.

The biggest concern is that a frightened cat may try to escape, while decorations, candy, and other seasonal hazards can create additional risks. A few simple changes around the home can help keep cats safe while everyone else enjoys the festivities.

Even households that don't celebrate Halloween can be affected by the extra noise and activity around the neighborhood. Excited children, unfamiliar costumes, barking dogs, loud music, and parties can create an unusually stressful environment for cats.

A frightened cat may bolt when strangers approach the house, and there's no guarantee it will head somewhere safe. A cat that escapes could become lost or run into traffic while trying to get away.

Sources indicate that keeping cats indoors is therefore one of the most vital Halloween precautions. Even cats that normally spend time outside should remain indoors, with windows and doors securely closed.

With trick-or-treaters arriving throughout the evening, the front door may open far more often than usual. Every time it does, there's another opportunity for a cat to slip outside unnoticed.

Keeping a cat in a separate room when visitors arrive can reduce the risk, particularly if several people are coming and going. Making sure your cat is microchipped and that the registration details are up to date also improves the chances of being reunited if they do escape.

The simplest approach is to keep your cat away from the entrance for the entire evening rather than relying on everyone to remember to watch out for it.

Recent findings suggest that halloween decorations can look appealing to curious cats, but anything within reach may become a potential plaything. Curious cats can chew decorations or swallow small pieces, so it's best to avoid edible decorations and keep other items out of reach.

Carved pumpkins lit with real candles need particular care. A cat could knock one over, risking burns or even starting a fire.

Battery-operated candles offer a safer alternative. Another option is to place pumpkins outside or in a window where the cat can't reach them.

It has been revealed that it can be tempting to dress a cat up for Halloween, especially when everyone else in the household is wearing a costume. However, many cats find clothing uncomfortable or frightening, and restrictive outfits can cause unnecessary stress.

Sources indicate that some cats need to wear garments for medical reasons, such as a surgical vest to protect stitches after an operation. Halloween costumes are different because they generally serve no practical purpose for the cat.

Pay attention to how a cat responds to clothing and accessories. If they seem uncomfortable or distressed, leave the costume off. There are plenty of ways to include a cat in the celebration without dressing them up.

Recent findings suggest that candy presents several potential hazards for cats. Chocolate and certain other sweets contain ingredients that can be toxic to pets, while wrappers can become choking hazards if swallowed. Even sweets that aren't directly poisonous aren't suitable cat treats, and excess sugar can contribute to health problems.

It has been revealed that crinkly plastic wrappers can be particularly tempting because they appeal to a cat's instinct to chase and play with small objects. Itâs all fun and games when a cat bats them around, but they could end up swallowing them.

Sources indicate that keep Halloween treats in a closed container somewhere the cat can't access, and make sure children understand that sharing their candy with pets isn't safe. If a cat manages to eat candy, contact a vet promptly for advice.

Recent findings suggest that cats often cope with stress by hiding somewhere they feel safe. Providing a quiet room away from visitors and noise gives them the chance to retreat until the activity dies down.

Industry observers note that A bedroom can work well, provided it has fresh water, a litter tray, and a favorite blanket or other familiar bedding. Guests should know that the room is off-limits so the cat isn't disturbed while resting.

Giving a cat this private space can be especially helpful during parties or evenings when the front door is opening repeatedly.

According to recent reports, it's sensible to check on a cat throughout Halloween, particularly when the household is busy. These checks help confirm that the cat is comfortable and hasn't slipped out unnoticed.

In a recent development, however, checking in doesn't mean coaxing a frightened cat out of its hiding place. If they have chosen a quiet spot and appear settled, let them stay there.

The aim is to make sure the cat is safe without adding more attention or activity when it would rather be left alone.

Sources indicate that keeping a cat safe doesn't mean they have to be excluded from the evening entirely. Cats that dislike costumes can still feature in a Halloween photoshoot without wearing anything themselves. After all, theyâre already wearing the best outfit! Dressing as a character known for having a feline companion is another way to include a cat without making them uncomfortable.

A scary movie marathon can also be a relaxed way to spend the evening together. A soft, Halloween-themed blanket and a favorite treat might encourage a cat to settle on a lap, provided it enjoys that kind of attention.

Cat-friendly treats can be offered while the humans enjoy their own candy, and cats that like catnip may appreciate a Halloween-themed toy with a little dried catnip.

Sources indicate that halloween should be enjoyable for the whole household, but cats don't understand why the neighborhood suddenly becomes noisier or why strangers keep appearing at the door. Keeping them indoors, removing potential hazards, and providing somewhere quiet to retreat can make the night safer and more comfortable for everyone.

  • When I got out of the pool, I walked over to my kids.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, twenty-four years. That’s how long it had been since I last stood atop a swim block, preparing to dive in for a timed race in an official meet.

According to recent reports, A whistle blew. The crowd hushed to silence. A monotone call came over the loudspeaker, “Swimmers, take your mark,” followed by a loud electronic beep that signaled the start of the race. I felt the cold rush of water overtake my body upon diving in. The neurons in my brain feverishly told my muscles to complete the strokes I’d learned decades before. In seconds, it was done. I finished the race.

When I got out of the pool, I walked over to my kids. My son, a competitive swimmer himself, looked at me and earnestly stated, “Wow, Mom. I’m proud of you.”.

Like most moms, I have a packed schedule. I work, parent, volunteer at school, shepherd my two kids to practices and social gatherings, throw meals together, walk the dog, and occasionally find a moment to breathe. But over the past couple of years, I watched my growing kids, now ages 12 and 9, discover and engage in passions that light them up. It left me wondering, why not me, too?

“A recurring theme in my practice is women feeling they’ve lost their individual identities somewhere between work, parenting, and meeting everyone else’s needs,” says Carly Snyder, a Upcoming York City–based reproductive and perinatal psychiatrist. “Part of my work involves helping women recognize that their own interests and needs are legitimate.”.

In a recent development, research highlights a multitude of benefits earned by pursuing hobbies. Hobbyists often have wider social networks, improved mental health markers, and enhanced positive emotions.

Industry observers note that hobbies offer a particularly important lifeline for mothers, who often report losing themselves to the demanding needs of family life. That rings true for Kaitlyn Edington, an art educator and mom of two who recalls struggling after returning to work as a teacher following the birth of her first child. “I was so depleted,” Edington claims. She spent her workdays teaching with short breaks to pump, often bringing her computer into her pumping room so she could catch up on work, then went home to full nights of infant care.

It has been revealed that one day while scrolling on Instagram, Edington saw an artist posting images of her sketchbook paintings. “She changed my life,” Edington says. “Her sketchbook paintings were so loose and free, and she was encouraging people to draw everyday. I remember thinking, ‘If I have to pump two to three times a day, which I absolutely hate, why not pair it with something that I love?’” From then on, Edington sketched when she pumped, and ultimately developed a habit of daily sketching that she continues 10 years later.

Sources indicate that no longer in the pumping phase of life, Edington ensures she gets time to sketch by waking up before her kids. “I hold the habit of waking up before my kids as sacred,” she says. “I need that time, when nobody needs me. It’s my emotional rest.”.

Science backs Edington’s belief that her hobby stabilizes her mental health. “Reengaging in meaningful, enjoyable activities can be therapeutically valuable,” Snyder indicates. “Behavioral activation, an evidence-based treatment for depression, specifically emphasizes reconnecting with activities that provide pleasure, purpose, or a sense of accomplishment.”.

Snyder has three children, ages 19, 16, and 11, and throughout their lives she has maintained her dedication to skiing, cycling, yoga and running, completing a total of 19 marathons. She knows her kids benefit from her hobbies. Each time Snyder trains for an upcoming marathon, “[My kids] witness my commitment, discipline, setbacks, and perseverance,” she claims. “Watching a parent pursue a hobby provides opportunities to observe persistence, emotional regulation, problem-solving, and enjoyment.”.

But those benefits are secondary to the impacts hobbies have on the women pursuing them. “I think we’ve become so accustomed to framing everything mothers do in terms of how it benefits their children,” Snyder notes. “Women are entitled to happiness and fulfillment for their own sake.”.

Industry observers note that it’s simply an added bonus that when mom is happy for mom’s sake, the benefits for her kids naturally follow, according to multiple studies linking a mother’s well-being with her child’s. Plus, kids also learn that all stages of adulthood, including those under the umbrella of parenting, can include personal fulfillment, curiosity, and growth.

The best way to start a hobby is to let yourself reconnect with something you already love. I remembered how much joy I got out of competing in swim meets in high school, and I was eager to recreate that glee. Ask yourself, “What did I love when I was a kid or a young adult?”.

Sources indicate that your hobby doesn’t have to involve intense commitment. “Reading, gardening, dancing, listening to music, or simply spending time alone can be just as meaningful as running a marathon,” Snyder notes.

Search online for local groups involved in the activity you want to pursue. Your local library may have resources to help you get started as well.

When you’re ready to commit, set realistic goals. Start by focusing on your hobby consistently for just 10-15 minutes per day. Showing up is the main goal.

Recent findings suggest that “Motherhood should expand a woman’s identity, not erase it,” Snyder advises. Which hobby will help expand yours?
